title: Double Categories
text:
Definition 1.1 (Double category)  A  double category  \(\mathbb{C}\) consists of the following data:

a category \(\mathbb{C}_0\), whose objects we call 0-cells, and whose arrows we call tight 1- cells \(f: V \rightarrow V'\);
a category \(\mathbb{C}_1\), whose objects we call loose 1-cells \(N: V \not\rightarrow W\), and whose arrows we call 2-cells





two functors \(\text{src}, \text{tgt} : \mathbb{C}_1 \rightarrow \mathbb{C}_0\) called source and target respectively;
composition and identity functors \(\text{comp} : \mathbb{C}_1 \times_{\mathbb{C}_0} \mathbb{C}_1\) and \(\text{id} : \mathbb{C}_0 \rightarrow \mathbb{C}_1\);
natural families of globular isomorphisms in \(\mathbb{C}_1\):


<LaTeX content not imagified>

\begin{tikzcd}
    V && Y \\
    & {\Downarrow a_{P,M,N}} \\
    V && Y
    \arrow["(P\circ M) \circ N"{inner sep=.8ex}, "\shortmid"{marking}, from=1-1, to=1-3]
    \arrow[equals, nfold, from=1-1, to=3-1]
    \arrow[equals, nfold, from=1-3, to=3-3]
    \arrow["P \circ (M \circ N)"'{inner sep=.8ex}, "\shortmid"{marking}, from=3-1, to=3-3]
\end{tikzcd}

<end of LaTeX content>


<LaTeX content not imagified>

\begin{tikzcd}
    W && X \\
    & {\Downarrow \ell_M} \\
    W && X
    \arrow["\text{id}_X \circ M"{inner sep=.8ex}, "\shortmid"{marking}, from=1-1, to=1-3]
    \arrow[equals, nfold, from=1-1, to=3-1]
    \arrow[equals, nfold, from=1-3, to=3-3]
    \arrow["M"'{inner sep=.8ex}, "\shortmid"{marking}, from=3-1, to=3-3]
\end{tikzcd}

<end of LaTeX content>


<LaTeX content not imagified>

\begin{tikzcd}
    W && X \\
    & {\Downarrow r_M} \\
    W && X
    \arrow["M \circ \text{id}_W"{inner sep=.8ex}, "\shortmid"{marking}, from=1-1, to=1-3]
    \arrow[equals, nfold, from=1-1, to=3-1]
    \arrow[equals, nfold, from=1-3, to=3-3]
    \arrow["M"'{inner sep=.8ex}, "\shortmid"{marking}, from=3-1, to=3-3]
\end{tikzcd}

<end of LaTeX content>

These data are required to satisfy the following coherence axioms which manifest as equations between composite 2-cells.
The first of these is the following composite

<LaTeX content not imagified>

\begin{tikzcd}
    V && Z \\
    & {\Downarrow a_{Q, P, M} \star \text{id}_N} \\
    V && Z\\
    & {\Downarrow a_{Q, P \circ M, N} }\\
    V && Z \\
    & {\Downarrow id_Q \star a_{P, M, N} }\\
    V && Z
    \arrow["((Q \circ P)\circ N) \circ M"{inner sep=.8ex}, "\shortmid"{marking}, from=1-1, to=1-3]
    \arrow[equals, nfold, from=1-1, to=3-1]
    \arrow[equals, nfold, from=1-3, to=3-3]
    \arrow["(Q \circ (P \circ M)) \circ N"'{inner sep=.8ex}, "\shortmid"{marking}, from=3-1, to=3-3]
    \arrow[equals, nfold, from=3-1, to=5-1]
    \arrow[equals, nfold, from=3-3, to=5-3]
    \arrow["Q \circ ((P \circ M) \circ N)"'{inner sep=.8ex}, "\shortmid"{marking}, from=5-1, to=5-3]
    \arrow[equals, nfold, from=5-1, to=7-1]
    \arrow[equals, nfold, from=5-3, to=7-3]
    \arrow["Q \circ (P \circ (M \circ N))"'{inner sep=.8ex}, "\shortmid"{marking}, from=7-1, to=7-3]
\end{tikzcd}

<end of LaTeX content>

which is required to be equal to the second composite

<LaTeX content not imagified>

\begin{tikzcd}
    V && Z \\
    & {\Downarrow a_{Q \circ P, M, N}} \\
    V && Z\\
    & {\Downarrow a_{Q, P, M \circ N} }\\
    V && Z \\
    \arrow["((Q \circ P)\circ N) \circ M"{inner sep=.8ex}, "\shortmid"{marking}, from=1-1, to=1-3]
    \arrow[equals, nfold, from=1-1, to=3-1]
    \arrow[equals, nfold, from=1-3, to=3-3]
    \arrow["(Q \circ P) \circ (M \circ N)"'{inner sep=.8ex}, "\shortmid"{marking}, from=3-1, to=3-3]
    \arrow[equals, nfold, from=3-1, to=5-1]
    \arrow[equals, nfold, from=3-3, to=5-3]
    \arrow["Q \circ ((P \circ M) \circ N)"'{inner sep=.8ex}, "\shortmid"{marking}, from=5-1, to=5-3]
\end{tikzcd}

<end of LaTeX content>
